children: The Serbian GDP expanded by 3.8% from the previous year in the second quarter of 2026, picking up from the 3.2% growth rate in the earlier period and revised higher from the preliminary estimate of 3.6%.

It was the sharpest expansion since the second quarter of 2024, underscoring the country's resilience to the economic shocks of higher energy prices and trade bottlenecks since the outbreak of war in the Middle East. Output soared for construction (9.1% vs -9.7% in Q1), agriculture, forestry, and fishing (12.1% vs 11.6%), financial and insurance services (5.2% vs 7.1%), and professional, scientific, and technical activities (5.8% vs 6.1%).
From the previous quarter, the Serbian GDP expanded by 1.5% on a seasonally adjusted basis, the most in three years.

title: Serbia GDP Growth Rises to 2-Year High
